transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get the pre-launch review started. As we know, the new search-ranking service is scheduled for its first production rollout on Thursday, June 12, at 14:00 UTC. The service passed staging tests, and the current launch plan starts with 25% of production search traffic. Before I finalize the launch checklist, I need to do a round-robin sign-off with platform engineering, customer support, and security. I also need to confirm three things for the checklist: the explicit initial traffic percentage, a p99 latency rollback threshold, and clearance of any critical dependency findings. Let's go around the room — platform engineering first, then customer support, then security. Please share any findings or concerns you have so we can determine whether we're clear to proceed.

Under the platform rollout policy, this means I must change the initial exposure to exactly 5% and set the automatic rollback threshold to exactly 750 ms. I have not yet filed the performance finding or updated the launch checklist.

transcript.text: I need to share a critical finding from customer support. I confirmed with the account team today that a major enterprise customer's contract requires 48 hours of advance notice and blocks search changes from 14:00 to 16:00 UTC. Notice was sent Wednesday at 10:00 UTC, so the first compliant launch slot is Friday, June 13, at exactly 16:00 UTC. This has not been added to the launch calendar yet. This means the currently scheduled Thursday June 12 at 14:00 UTC rollout is not compliant with the contractual notice window and falls within the blocked time period.
